requirements.description: CRSP daily stock returns for MAX signal construction (avg of 5 highest daily returns in month).
CRSP monthly stock returns for portfolio formation and FM regressions.
CRSP point-in-time universe for share-code (10/11) and exchange-code (1/2/3) filters, plus SIC code for utility/financial exclusions.
Delisting returns for surviving CRSP universe; needed for performance persistence (Shumway/BMP-style treatment when dlret is missing).
CRSP-Compustat link for merging fundamentals into the stock panel.
Compustat annual fundamentals for book equity (BE = SEQ + TXDB + ITCB - PSTKRV/PSTKL/PSTK), ROA, asset growth, and SIC code for industry exclusions.
Compustat quarterly fundamentals for IBQ (ROE) and lagged book equity (1-quarter lag).
Fama-French three-factor monthly (MKT-RF, SMB, HML) for FF3 alphas.
Carhart momentum factor (WML) needed for FFC4 / FF6 / FF6PS construction (Mom not in five_factor).
Fama-French five-factor monthly (MKT-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA) for FF5/FF6 alphas.
Monthly risk-free rate for excess-return computation.
Market portfolio daily/monthly returns for the CAPM alpha regression.
Pre-computed daily market-beta on 252-day rolling window — used directly for MAX^beta construction (each month, sort stocks into beta deciles, then MAX within beta).
13F institutional holdings data (Thomson Reuters) for INST variable (% shares held by institutions at quarter-end) and INST terciles in Table 9.

Pastor-Stambaugh (2003) traded liquidity factor (LIQ). Required for FFCPS and FF6PS alpha columns in Tables 1, 6, and Table 9 FF6PS column. Paper explicitly sources it from Robert Stambaugh's website.
Stambaugh-Yuan (2017) mispricing factors (MGMT, PERF). Required for SY alpha columns in Tables 1, 6, and Table 9. Paper explicitly sources them from Robert Stambaugh's website.

Daniel-Hirshleifer-Sun (2020) behavioral factors (FIN, PEAD). Required for DHS alpha columns in Tables 1, 6, and Table 9. Paper explicitly sources them from Lin Sun's website. DHS-only sample starts Jul 1972.

blocking_issues.reason: Pastor-Stambaugh (2003) LIQ factor is not present in the FF database or anywhere in the ClickHouse catalog. The paper sources it directly from Robert Stambaugh's website.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Drop FFCPS and FF6PS alpha columns from Tables 1, 6, and the FF6PS alpha column from Table 9 Panel B. These cells will be closed-vocab-marker FAILs (documented in assumptions.md with [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET]). The headline MAX^beta effect is still testable via FF3/FF5/FF6 alphas, which are available; the FF6PS column in Table 9 is replaced by the RET-RF column (already in metrics) so the heterogeneity test remains meaningful.

blocking_issues.reason: Stambaugh-Yuan (2017) MGMT and PERF factors are not in the FF database. The paper sources them from Robert Stambaugh's website.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Drop the SY alpha column from Tables 1 and 6. Mark as [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET] in assumptions.md. The mispricing-interpretation claim (C2) is still testable via the FF6PS column drop (already noted above) plus the MIS/CE firm-level characteristics in Table 2.

blocking_issues.reason: Daniel-Hirshleifer-Sun (2020) FIN and PEAD factors are not in the FF database. The paper sources them from Lin Sun's website. DHS analysis is restricted to Jul 1972 - Dec 2022 even with data.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Drop the DHS alpha column from Tables 1 and 6. Mark as [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET] in assumptions.md.
